chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from the one who narrated it, from Yahya ibn al-Mubarak, from Abdullah ibn Jabala, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, who said:

I said to him (peace be upon him): A poor man gifts me a gift, exposing himself to what is in my presence, so I take it and do not give him anything. Is it permissible for me? He (peace be upon him) said: Yes, it is permissible for you, but do not leave out giving him.

key_terms.لَا تَدَعْ: do not leave out / do not neglect

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to accept a gift from a poor person without giving them anything in return?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Kafi, the Imam clarifies that accepting a gift from a poor person who offers it to show respect or seek favor is legally permissible (halal) even if no reciprocal gift is given, distinguishing legal obligation from ethical virtue. This ruling highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on preserving the dignity of the giver while encouraging generosity as a means of strengthening social bonds. The hadith thus balances strict legal permissibility with the moral imperative of maintaining good relations through reciprocal kindness.
